nodes.title: Index of the scheme/adic/diamond comparison theorems available from the read sources, with their exact hypotheses (ECD 27.1-27.7, Huber 3.7.2, 3.8.1)
nodes.statement: Scheme -> diamond (characteristic p, ECD): c_X^* commutes with ⊗̂ and pullback (27.1); c_X^*: D_ét(X,Λ) -> D_ét(X^◇,Λ) is fully faithful with right adjoint Rc_{X*} (27.2, any scheme of characteristic p, Λ I-adic with I regular containing an integer prime to p); Rc_{X*} commutes with RHom and pushforward (27.3); for f separated of finite type between qcqs schemes of characteristic p (or perfections), Rf^◇_! c_Y^* ≅ c_X^* Rf_! and Rf^! Rc_{X*} ≅ Rc_{Y*} R(f^◇)^! (27.4). Scheme -> diamond (mixed characteristic over a complete DVR O with perfect residue field, ECD): the same Rf_!/Rf^! comparison for separated f between schemes of finite type over O (27.5); commutation of c^* with Rf_* on constructible complexes for finite Λ killed by an integer prime to p (27.6); full faithfulness on constructible complexes (27.7). Scheme -> adic (Huber): for f proper between schemes locally of finite type over a scheme S and φ: R -> S from an adic space, the base change φ_Y^* R^+f_* -> R^+f^ad_* φ_X^* is an isomorphism for torsion Λ (3.7.2); for f of finite type between schemes locally of finite type over a complete non-archimedean field k and F constructible Z/nZ with n prime to char k, the comparison R^q f_* F -> R^q f^rig_* F is bijective (3.8.1, proofs delegated). None of these is a diamond six-operations construction; each transports a scheme construction under the listed hypotheses, as the stage requires.
hypotheses: As listed per theorem; the cycle-class/trace/orientation comparisons and the pro-étale rational duality of the stage were not read

nodes.title: Poincaré duality for a lisse Q_ℓ-sheaf on an open of a smooth projective curve with j_* (Weil I Théorème 2.12): statement and import boundary
nodes.statement: For X a projective smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field k, U ⊆ X the complement of finitely many closed points, j: U -> X and F a lisse Q_ℓ-sheaf on U, the pairing Tr(x ∪ y): H^i(X, j_*F) ⊗ H^{2−i}(X, j_*F^∨(1)) -> H^2(X, Q_ℓ(1)) ≅ Q_ℓ is a perfect duality. Deligne's remark (2.14 E): this follows from the general duality theorem SGA 4 XVIII (3.2.5) (with S = Spec k, K = j_*F, L = Q_ℓ) by a local computation 'qui n'est pas difficile'; for tamely ramified F it can be obtained transcendentally by lifting to characteristic 0. The stalks of j_*F at the missing points are the local-monodromy invariants (2.11).
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; X projective smooth connected curve; F lisse Q_ℓ on U (torsion version first, Q_ℓ by formal limits per (2.14 A))
The proof is not in Weil I; SGA 4 XVIII 3.2.5 (in the library as Weil_SGA4_XVII_XVIII.txt) was not read
proofSteps: Import SGA 4 XVIII 3.2.5 and perform the local computation at the points of X − U.
acceptance: Used in Weil I (3.9) and Weil II (3.3.5) to turn upper weight bounds into lower bounds; the pairing is the one on j_*F, not on j_!F.

sources.excerpt: Théorème (2.12). — La forme bilinéaire Tr(x ∪ y) : H^i(X, j_*F) ⊗ H^{2−i}(X, j_*F^∨(1)) -> H^2(X, j_*F ⊗ j_*F^∨(1)) -> H^2(X, j_*(F ⊗ F^∨)(1)) -> H^2(X, j_*Q_ℓ(1)) = H^2(X, Q_ℓ(1)) -> Q_ℓ est une dualité parfaite.
sources.match: Statement (the displayed pairing is reconstructed from the OCR fragments).

sources.excerpt: La forme (2.12) du théorème de dualité de Poincaré résulte du résultat général SGA 4, XVIII (3.2.5) ... par un calcul local qui n'est pas difficile. L'énoncé figurera explicitement dans la version définitive de SGA 5.

gaps.title: Integration consequence: three of this packet's supplier links are not yet stage edges
gaps.detail: Added by independent review. EDC.6's atlas description does license these links - it says 'Through AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2-L6 prove the applicable scheme/adic/diamond operation comparisons, preserving the source's qcqs, finite-dimensional and l-invertibility hypotheses' - but EDC.6's requires list is ['AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2', 'AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5', 'AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L6', ...], which contains neither L3 nor L4, and contains no ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology stage at all. Integrating this packet therefore adds three stage edges: L3 -> EDC.6, L4 -> EDC.6 and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5 -> EDC.6. A reachability check over data/atlas.json stageEdges confirms all three are acyclic. The seventh link, EDC.2 -> DWP.2, already exists as a stage edge (DWP.2 requires EDC.2), so it needs no new edge. ORCHESTRATOR DECISION: add the three edges, or widen EDC.6's requires list, or route the L3/L4/H5 material through L2/L5/L6.

review.notes: This is a deliberately thin packet - two nodes, both assembled from sources read for other roadmaps - and it says so in its own summary. Both nodes, all their locators and excerpts, and all seven links were checked. Sources: EtCohDiamonds.pdf, SUP_Huber_EtaleCohomology_1996.pdf and SS_WeilI.pdf, all from the supplied library with SHA-256 matching references/CATALOGUE.json. Page conventions: EtCohDiamonds printed = PDF page; Huber printed = PDF - 10; Weil I printed = PDF + 271. All 2 parentStageId values and all 13 coverage stageId values exist in data/atlas.json and are owned by EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves; eleven of the thirteen stages are honestly marked not_read. Implementation status left unchecked. CORRECTION. Weil I Théorème (2.12) is printed on p. 283, not p. 282: page 282 ends with item (2.11) (the stalk of j_*F at a missing point as local-monodromy invariants), and (2.12) is the second item on p. 283. Locator fixed, and the one-fragment excerpt ('est une dualité parfaite') was replaced by the full printed statement of the pairing, read from the scan. LINKS. Six links have as SOURCE a node of a sibling packet in this job - four from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons (L3 x2, L4, L6) and two from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology (H5 x2); all six node ids were checked and exist. The seventh runs from this packet's EDC.2 node INTO a node of DeligneWeightsAndPurity. Every direction and scope claim was checked against the atlas stage texts. EDC.6's description licenses the first six ('Through AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2-L6 prove the applicable scheme/adic/diamond operation comparisons'), and DWP.2's requires list does contain EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2, so the seventh is consistent with an existing stage edge. The seventh's mathematical claim was independently confirmed: a 150 dpi rendering of Weil I printed p. 286 shows that the proof of Corollary (3.9) does use Poincaré duality (2.12) to produce the lower bound q^{(beta+1)/2 - 1/2} <= |alpha|. A NEW GAP records that L3 -> EDC.6, L4 -> EDC.6 and H5 -> EDC.6 are not yet stage edges (acyclic if added). CHECKED AND CONFIRMED, not corrected: the EDC.6 index node's summary of ECD 27.1-27.7 and Huber 3.7.2/3.8.1 agrees, hypothesis by hypothesis, with what I verified directly in the AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology packets - in particular the restriction of 27.6-27.7 to finite coefficients killed by an integer prime to p, the qcqs and finite-type hypotheses of 27.4 and 27.5, and the torsion hypothesis of Huber 3.7.2. The node is explicitly an INDEX with a cross-reference proof step, not a second proof, which is the right shape for a stage whose description calls the material 'transport of the scheme construction, not a second construction of diamond six operations'. The EDC.2 node's record that Weil I does not prove (2.12) - Deligne delegates it to SGA 4 XVIII (3.2.5) plus a local computation, adding 'L'énoncé figurera explicitement dans la version définitive de SGA 5' - is exact, and the (2.14 E) excerpt was verified at printed p. 283.

checked.note: Both excerpts (ECD Proposition 27.6 at printed p. 166; Huber Theorem 3.7.2 at printed p. 226) match verbatim, and the node's hypothesis-by-hypothesis index of ECD 27.1-27.7 and Huber 3.7.2/3.8.1 agrees with what was verified directly in the two sibling packets. The node correctly presents itself as an index, not a second proof.

Théorème (2.12) is on printed p. 283, not p. 282; p. 282 ends with (2.11). Locator fixed and the one-fragment excerpt replaced by the full printed statement. The (2.14 E) delegation to SGA 4 XVIII (3.2.5), including the sentence about the definitive version of SGA 5, was verified at printed p. 283, and the node's record that the proof is NOT in Weil I is exact.
